reference: I. Krasikov, J. C. Lagarias, Bounds for the 3x+1 problem using difference inequalities, Acta Arith. 109 (2003) 237-258, arXiv:math/0205002, Thm 2.2
claim: L^NT_4(lambda) is feasible for lambda = 1.6122, hence pi_a(x) >= x^gamma for every gamma < log2(lambda) and x >= x0(a, gamma)
check: index i in [0, N) is the residue m = 3i+2 mod 3^k, n3 = N/3. For every i, with j, t = divmod(i, 3), cbar(r) = min(C[r], C[r+n3], C[r+2n3]): C[i]*D <= q*C[(4i+2) mod N] + L*cbar(r), where L = L2, r = 4j mod n3 if t = 0; L = 0 if t = 1; L = L1, r = (2j+1) mod n3 if t = 2. Requires q/D <= lambda^-2, L2/D <= lambda^(alpha-2), L1/D <= lambda^(alpha-1), alpha = log2(3), and C >= 1.
